Stages: what is on main, what is waiting, and why

Status as of 2026-10-06 (UTC). One row per stage, merged or not. The gate for each stage is the row in architecture.md; this file records the result, where the evidence is, and what still blocks a merge or a cutover. Update a row when its branch lands or its gate changes.

On main: gpu-guard, remote4k and watcher, then in round 3 details, subtitles, rename, collections, posters, health and audit, one at a time in that order, then jfsync in round 5 (merge ad20269), then lists from the Letterboxd batch (merge ea80286), then the subtitles cheap-first rework (merge 01031af), then tonight from the Letterboxd batch round 3 (merge ef45864), then three owner-approved tweaks one at a time: no-ssdmirror (merge 836a4df: the ssdmirror stage, merged in round 1, is deleted; the SSD copy is a one-time copy for a friend, not pipeline work), plex-speed (merge 536bdb5: health times Plex's hubs and optimizes its database; see health) and lists-top500 (merge 280643e: see lists), then letterboxd from the Letterboxd batch round 7 (merge 4e8dd24), then the collection posters (merge d3fb5b2: see posters), then fix/batch-1 (merge d50bc34: a run a shutdown or restart cuts off is recorded interrupted, see the deploy notes below, plus fixes in remote4k, details, posters and letterboxd, see their rows), then llm/gateway (merge 599e4f0: see llm), then fix/batch-2 (merge cbaf2c2: see letterboxd; plus a scheduler test that a stage's own wrapped context.Canceled with the service alive is recorded error), feat/nvme-guards (merge 592b823: see health and appbackup) and feat/letterboxd-people (merge 4d3c021: see letterboxd), one at a time in that order, then feat/tonight-household (merge 4ae59d0: tonight becomes a household row, see tonight; letterboxd shares its feed read, reader and export with it), then feat/plex-watchlists (merge 681b72a: each member's Letterboxd watchlist on their own Plex watchlist, and no server Watchlist collection; see letterboxd). Also on main: the shared TMDB, fanart.tv and AI gateway (internal/llm) clients, internal/watch (projectionist's own watch record, from jfsync; the diary's logged kind and played_at, from letterboxd) and internal/lbpace (one Letterboxd pace for the whole process, from lists). A sidecar with 1-39 cues is unjudged, not "not an SRT". On 13 library titles (5 archived laugh-track sidecars, 6 verified films, an animated episode, a Colin from Accounts episode): every verified film still fits, 3 archived sidecars now fit at 0.0 s, 2 stay unjudged. LLM calls: the AI gateway

Every model call (the posters and collection judges, tonight's picks) goes through the Vercel AI Gateway's OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API (https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1) on [llm] key_file, secrets/ai_gateway_api_key, unless its task names an API of its own (below); a key is read on every request. [llm] in the config sets the gateway and each task; config.example.toml lists the defaults.

The vision tasks send effort "none", not "off": "off" asks for the least the first model allows, and a fallback may read it differently (qwen3-vl-instruct has no reasoning control, so behind it qwen3.7-flash would reason). qwen3-vl-instruct and qwen3.7-flash answered a live call with "reasoning": {"effort": "none"} (2026-10-06T02Z, HTTP 200; 0 reasoning tokens), and so did gpt-5.6-luna and claude-opus-5.5 (2026-10-06T04Z; 0 reasoning tokens). tonight's "off" sends effort "none" too, which both of its models list.

Each task may list fallbacks: the gateway tries them in order when the model fails (its models field), and the answer names the model that served it. A task table that leaves fallbacks out keeps the default's; fallbacks = [] means none. A Claude model is just another id (anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5); there is no second client.

A task on an API of its own. A task table may set api and key_file (OpenAI's own API, https://api.openai.com/v1, for the one-time poster pass on GPT-6 Astra on the one-time key) and must then set price_in and price_out, USD per million input and output tokens: no catalogue prices it, so a call costs its tokens at those prices (input read from OpenAI's prompt cache counted in full), and a lost answer counts at that worst case. It sends OpenAI's plain Chat Completions body: no models, reasoning or message cache_control (OpenAI refuses an unknown field with HTTP 400, and caches prefixes by itself), max_completion_tokens for max_tokens (which OpenAI's reasoning models refuse), and the effort as written, as reasoning_effort; "off" sends none, leaving the model's default, as no catalogue says what the model's least is. GPT-6 Astra takes low, medium, high, xhigh and max (OpenAI's model page, read 2026-10-06), so its tasks set reasoning = "low". A missing price, or any fallback (only the gateway tries them: set fallbacks = []), fails the config load with an error naming the task. Moving the task back to the gateway is deleting those four keys. in_flight stays one bound across every API.

Throughput and failure policy (internal/llm):

  • at most in_flight (8) calls in the air across the process; posters fans out that wide;
  • each attempt has timeout (120 s); 429, 5xx, timeouts and dropped connections are retried with jittered backoff (2-4 s, 4-8 s, 8-16 s) or after the gateway's Retry-After, up to attempts (4) in all; a Retry-After over 5 minutes fails the call at once; any other answer (400, 401, 404) fails it at once;
  • a stage's run parks a task after park_after (5) failed calls in a row: no more calls this run, one alert;
  • a billing refusal (402; a 403 for no card on file, customer_verification_required, or for a model outside the free tier, "Free tier users do not have access to this model"; or OpenAI's 429 insufficient_quota, which waiting does not end, so it is never retried) parks the task at once. It holds back only the tasks on its account, its API and key: the one-time OpenAI key out of quota leaves tonight calling on the gateway. It is kept in the store (since when, the last refused call, whether it was told) until a call is answered again, and while it stands:
    • one alert in all, naming since when, raised by the first stage that meets it (TellBilling, the stored "told" pattern of the scheduler's once-only alerts); later runs, other stages and restarts only log judge_billing_held / tonight_billing_held;
    • no call is sent but one an hour (billingRecheck), across the process and its restarts: every other session is parked before it calls (posters writes no ledger row for it), and the callers that reach the hourly try wait for its answer, going on if it was answered and held if it was refused again (callers already waiting then get a $0 failed ledger row). So a refused account costs at most 24 free calls a day, and the stages resume within an hour of the owner fixing billing;
    • it is no model failure: it bills nothing, holds nothing against a budget, and does not count towards a title's unusable answers;
  • an answer that cannot be read is asked once more in the same run; posters then marks the title unjudged (two unusable answers, as before); tonight keeps its one-retry rule. A "reason" inside "scores" is ignored, not fatal.

Cost and budgets. A call's cost is the gateway's own figure when the answer carries one, else its usage at the dearest price the gateway may bill for the model (a task on an API of its own: its usage at its own prices). That price is the highest of the model list's prices (GET /v1/models: base, regional, fast and tiered) and every provider's (GET /v1/models/<id>/endpoints), each at its peak multiplier; both are fetched once a day for every model a task names and cached in the store, since the gateway picks the provider. The providers matter: a live call to deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 (2026-10-06T01:12Z) was served by alibaba and billed $0.44 / $1.32 per million tokens, its $0.22 / $0.66 doubled in its peak window (00:00-14:00 UTC), where the model list says $0.13 / $0.26. Before a call, its worst case (the input estimate, at 3 bytes a token plus each image's 28-pixel patches, and all of max_tokens as output, at the dearest price among the task's models) is reserved against the stage's cap: posters' budget_usd and collection_budget_usd, tonight's daily_cap_usd. An attempt sent in full whose answer was lost counts at that worst case even when a retry answers. posters_calls records the model that answered, its tokens and its cost.

The reservation is one attempt's worst case, as specified, so a cap is hard for new calls but not for lost answers: a call that loses answers after sending them in full counts each lost attempt at its worst case, so the spend can pass the cap by at most in_flight × (attempts − 1) worst cases, and the next call is then refused. For posters on alibaba/qwen3-vl-instruct (dearest $0.40 / $1.60 per million, alibaba's; its fallback's dearest tier is $0.20 / $0.80) that is 8 × 3 × $0.0021 ≈ $0.05: a six-candidate title estimates about 1,270 input tokens (387 for the prompt, 6 × 126 image patches for 252×392 thumbnails, the framing) plus all 1,024 output tokens. On the dearest bake-off model, alibaba/qwen3.8-27b ($0.99 / $4.35), it is about $0.14. tonight's pair is sized the same way and logs tonight_over_cap when lost answers pass it.

The cost figure is usage.cost, else provider_metadata.gateway.cost (the message's, else the answer's). The Chat Completions docs (fetched 2026-10-06) show no cost field, but the live answer of 2026-10-06T01:12Z carries usage.cost as a number and the metadata's as a decimal string ("cost": "0.00000572", beside marketCost, inferenceCost and the routing); Opus's answers of 2026-10-06T04Z carry only usage.cost. usage.cost is what the gateway billed: it prices input read from the prompt cache at the cache's rate, where usage at the list price counts it in full (twice the real cost of an Opus judge call with the taste references). A figure is read when it is a number or a decimal string, with or without "$"; any other shape (an object, text with units, a metadata that is not an object) counts as no figure, never as an unreadable answer that would be asked again and paid twice.

The bake-off (cmd/bakeoff, a tool, not a test) sends each candidate model exactly what the stage would: 60 titles drawn from a copy of the production store with stored Sonnet verdicts (owner picks and Plex defaults; uploads are never judged, so none has one), movies, shows and seasons, plus hard cases (alt art he picked that Sonnet ranked lower, a pool with a non-English poster, verdicts that turned on text or clutter); and tonight's prompt as the stage sizes it. It reports per model: % valid answers, top-1 agreement with Sonnet (a tie with Sonnet's pick agrees), the mean Spearman of the scores, how often its top pick is one Sonnet scored 4 or less, cost per title, p50/p95 latency, and a contact sheet of its disagreements; for tonight, validity and the picks with their reasons. Its doc comment has the commands; -fake runs it on the fake gateway, and -max-usd (default $1) caps a live run. A title not sent (past -max-usd, or held by a billing refusal) is counted in a "not sent" column, never as an invalid answer or a $0 title: validity and cost per title count the titles sent. The owner's picks are drawn with rule owner_pick too (fix/batch-1 stores them so, Sonnet's scores kept). The client keeps its catalogue and any billing refusal in <out>/llm.db, not in the production copy, so a refusal stored there cannot hold a run back after billing is fixed.
